reason: This passage (Genesis 39-40) narrates the personal story of Joseph in Egypt—his service to Potiphar, the false accusation against him, his imprisonment, and his interpretation of dreams. The narrative focuses entirely on Joseph as an individual and his relationships with Egyptian officials. There is no depiction of the Hebrew people as a collective group, no expression of complaints, and no reference to Hebrew leaders or grievances against them. The only 'complaint' present is Potiphar's wife's false accusation against Joseph, which is unrelated to the statement's requirements.
